meta.name: Auto-fix ClickUp bug reports with OpenAI, Cursor, GitHub and Slack

parameters.content:
## AI Autonomous Bug-Fixing Pipeline

### How it works

This workflow receives ClickUp bug reports through a webhook, normalizes the bug details, and uses an OpenAI-powered agent to identify the root cause and propose a fix plan. It scores whether the issue is safe for autonomous fixing, routes uncertain cases through Slack developer approval, then sends the approved fix task to a Cursor background agent. After Cursor completes the fix and tests, the workflow prepares follow-up payloads, creates a GitHub pull request, updates the ClickUp task, and returns a success response.

### Setup steps

- Configure the ClickUp webhook to send new bug reports to the n8n webhook URL, and ensure the incoming payload contains the bug ID, task name, description, and stack trace fields expected by the config node.
- Add OpenAI credentials for the chat model used by the AI Agent node.
- Configure Slack credentials and the target channel or user for manual review notifications.
- Set the Cursor API URL and authentication details used by the HTTP Request node to trigger the Cursor background agent.
- Configure the wait/resume URLs or callback handling so developer approvals and Cursor completion events can resume the workflow correctly.
- Add GitHub credentials with permission to create pull requests in the target repository, and configure ClickUp credentials with permission to update bug task status.

### Customization

Adjust the auto-fix eligibility scoring logic, Slack approval message, Cursor task payload, target repository/branch, and ClickUp status values to match the team’s risk tolerance and development process.

## Receive bug report

Starts the workflow when ClickUp reports a bug and extracts the core bug fields into a normalized configuration object.

## Analyze fix eligibility

Uses the OpenAI-backed AI agent to analyze the bug, then parses, validates, normalizes, and scores the proposed fix plan for autonomous handling.

## Review approval path

Branches based on the auto-fix score; eligible items continue automatically while lower-confidence bugs notify a developer in Slack and wait for approval before proceeding.

## Run Cursor agent

Builds the Cursor background-agent task payload, triggers the Cursor API, and waits for the fix and test completion callback.

## Publish fix results

Parses the Cursor completion result, prepares PR and ClickUp payloads, creates a GitHub pull request, updates the ClickUp bug task, and sends the final webhook response.

parameters.text:
=You are a senior software engineer diagnosing a bug reported in ClickUp task {{ $json.bugId }} for repository {{ $json.repoUrl }} (branch {{ $json.repoBranch }}).

Bug title: {{ $json.taskName }}
Priority: {{ $json.priority }}

Description:
{{ $json.description }}

Stack trace / logs (if any):
{{ $json.stackTrace }}

Analyze this bug and determine:
- rootCause: the underlying cause of the bug, in plain language
- affectedFiles: array of specific file paths in the repository most likely involved in the fix
- fixApproach: a concrete description of the code change strategy to resolve it
- fixComplexity: one of low, medium, high
- confidence: a number from 0 to 1 estimating how confident you are that an automated coding agent could safely implement this fix without human intervention
- testPlan: which existing tests should verify the fix, and any new test cases that should be added
- riskFlags: array of short strings flagging any sensitive areas this fix touches (e.g. "auth", "payment", "database migration", "encryption", "user permissions") — empty array if none apply

Return ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no commentary) with exactly these keys: rootCause, affectedFiles, fixApproach, fixComplexity, confidence, testPlan, riskFlags.
